t: Section 7 of the Export-Import Bank Act of 1945 (12 U.S.C. 635f) is amended by striking “2011” and inserting “2014”.

fable.w: This section only changes a date in the Export-Import Bank Act, extending the Bank's authority from 2011 to 2014. The tempting reading is that reauthorizing the Bank implicitly carries forward advisory or consultative processes found elsewhere in that Act, but nothing in this section itself creates or requires consultation, comment, hearings, rulemaking, or a right to sue involving any party outside the federal government.
fable.s: is amended by striking “2011” and inserting “2014”

qwen_block.w: This section is a simple technical amendment that updates a year in a statute. It does not establish any process for consultation, public comment, advisory boards, or coordination with outside parties. It involves no interaction with entities outside the federal government.
qwen_block.s: Section 7 of the Export-Import Bank Act of 1945 (12 U.S.C. 635f) is amended by striking “2011” and inserting “2014”.

opus.w: The section only replaces "2011" with "2014" in Section 7 of the Export-Import Bank Act, which extends the Bank's authority. It does not create a way for anyone outside the federal government to take part in a federal decision. Linking the Bank to its outside customers would be reading in something the text doesn't say, and nothing in this section is even on-topic.
opus.b: 1. **Tempting-but-wrong reading:** The Export-Import Bank works with outside parties such as exporters and lenders, so you might think this section touches on outside involvement. It doesn't. The amendment only changes a date in Section 7 of the Act, which sets when the Bank's authority ends, from 2011 to 2014. It sets up no consultation, comment period, hearing, advisory body or right to sue.
